A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PODS research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, algorithms, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original GSM8K and MATH training experiments, accuracy and runtime comparisons, ablations, and appendix completion-length measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds model configurations, hardware timing measurements, speedup calculations and completion-length results.

M1.justification: The PODS procedure, subset-based advantage normalization, GRPO-PODS objective and max-variance selection algorithm remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. Expanded reward and batching descriptions document implementation rather than establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K and MATH for verifiable mathematical reasoning. The added model families, parameter scales and GPU configurations retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain GRPO or GRPO-GA as baselines, and the selection-rule comparison retains max-reward and random down-sampling. Newly cited SRPO, Reinforce-Rej and Polaris are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama3.2-3B/L40S and Qwen2.5-7B/eight-A100 configurations, an eight-A100 timing sweep over 8–1024 rollouts per GPU, and a speedup metric targeting 99% of baseline peak accuracy. For the retained Qwen3B/H100 experiment, reported sequence length changes from 1536 to 2048 and learning rate from 5e-6 to 2e-5. These reported setting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 1 directly investigates inference/update scaling and memory limits, substantially extending the analysis of the central computational bottleneck. Appendix A.4 adds time-to-target speedup analysis, and completion-length diagnostics cover the new configurations. Existing rollout/update-size and selection-rule ablations remain; the latter moves from Section 4.3 to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Accuracy and completion-length plots retain shading defined as 1.96 times the standard error of the mean. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v3 introduces no stated change to uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds accuracy, runtime and completion-length results for Llama3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-7B. Figure 1 reports a 21-fold reduction in per-token inference time between 8 and 512 rollouts. Table 3 newly reports speedups of 2.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.7 and 1.7 times for settings (a–e), using the 99%-peak target. Previously plotted accuracy and completion-length series are retained.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.1, Theorems 1–2 and their proofs retain the same mathematical content, including the extreme-reward subset characterization, O(n log n) algorithm and binary-reward special case.

C1.justification: The central PODS and max-variance contributions remain. The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace qualitative efficiency claims with an explicit minimum 1.7-fold speedup claim and extend the empirical claim to multiple model architectures and scales.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds practical recommendations favoring down-sampling ratios of 2–4 and describing ratios up to 16 as viable, extending v2's more cautious discussion of very small update sizes. The mathematical-task, prompt-diversity and off-policy limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies symbolic correctness verification, exact formatting requirements and tag-count reward values. Appendix A.2 consolidates settings for five configurations and explains microbatching, gradient accumulation and effective rollout/update sizes. These substantially expand implementation documentation, although v2's explicit evaluation intervals are omitted. The code access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SRPO, Reinforce-Rej and Polaris and more explicitly positions PODS against prompt selection and filtering. References for OpenAI o1, LoRA, Qwen2.5 and Llama3.2 are also added. The existing novelty claim about principled rollout down-sampling remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, parameter-selection discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The selection-rule comparison moves into an appendix reorganized into five subsections, the broader-impact paragraph is removed, and citations switch to author-date style.

P2.justification: v3 adds the timing figure and three tables, expands the main comparison and corresponding completion-length figure from three to five configurations, and revises the schematic's signal labels. Retained plots are substantially compressed vertically, with revised axes and legend placement, alongside document-wide layout changes.

improvement.justification: The phase profiling and additional model configurations strengthen the existing efficiency evidence, while Appendices A.1–A.2 improve implementation transparency. These gains are tempered by unexplained H100 setting revisions accompanying retained curves and lost evaluation-cadence documentation. The headline claim also describes reaching peak accuracy, whereas Appendix A.4 measures reaching 99% of that peak.
